title: 13-Year-Old Yu Zidi Storms to Third Gold — and a New Asian Games Record
summary:
Most 13-year-olds are worrying about homework. Yu Zidi is busy rewriting record books.

The Chinese swimmer dominated the 400m individual medley at the Asian Games in Nagoya, Japan, leading from the first stroke to the final touch. Her time — four minutes 28.56 seconds — smashed a Games record that had stood since 2014 by nearly 4.5 seconds. That's an eternity in swimming, where races are often decided by hundredths of a second.

Yu finished 3.95 seconds ahead of her compatriot Ke Wenxi, who took silver. Japan's Mio Narita claimed bronze. Only Canada's Summer McIntosh, the world record holder, has swum faster this year — Yu's time ranks as the fourth fastest in the world in 2025.

It's her third gold of these Games. She already won the 200m butterfly and 200m individual medley, both in Games record times. Suddenly, the 2028 Los Angeles Olympics don't seem so far away — and Yu is already being tipped as a medal contender.

There was another record-breaking moment in Nagoya too. North Korea's Ri Song Gum, 28, broke three world records on her way to a third Asian Games gold in the women's 49kg weightlifting category. The defending champion lifted 94kg in the snatch and 121kg in the clean-and-jerk — each 1kg above the previous world bests — for a total of 215kg, 4kg more than the old world record.

"The world record and this gold medal hold great meaning for me, because of everything I poured into this competition," Ri said. "I stepped out on to the competition floor today carrying that faith and those expectations."

Two athletes, two countries, one unforgettable week in Japan.
why_it_matters: Youth records force sport to confront hard questions about how early elite training should begin and who protects a 13-year-old under international pressure. At the same time, Yu's results signal a possible shift in swimming's balance of power and hand China a genuine medal hope for the 2028 Los Angeles Olympics.

background_read: The Asian Games is a multi-sport event for athletes from across Asia, organised by the Olympic Council of Asia and held every four years. It is often described as the second-largest multi-sport event in the world after the Olympics.

The individual medley is swimming's all-round test: competitors swim butterfly, backstroke, breaststroke and freestyle in a single race, so a swimmer has to be strong in all four rather than specialising in one.

Summer McIntosh (the Canadian swimmer who holds the world record in the 400m individual medley) is the benchmark Yu Zidi is chasing — and at 13, Yu still has years of physical development ahead of her.

Weightlifting has two lifts. In the snatch, the bar travels from the floor to overhead in one movement; in the clean-and-jerk, the lifter first brings the bar to the shoulders and then drives it up. An athlete's total is the sum of their best snatch and best clean-and-jerk.
Nagoya is a major city in central Japan and the host of these Games.

perspectives.perspective: Positive — China and the rise of young talent
perspectives.description: Yu's three golds, all in Games record times, show a talent pipeline working at a very high level. For Chinese swimming, it means a home-grown star who can compete globally for the next decade, and for the sport it is a genuinely exciting story.

perspectives.perspective: Critical — the cost of early stardom
perspectives.description: A 13-year-old is already being measured against world records and Olympic expectations, which raises concerns about burnout, injury and the loss of a normal childhood. The pressure to keep improving every single season can be brutal for athletes whose bodies are still changing.

perspectives.perspective: Neutral — the history of teenage prodigies
perspectives.description: Swimming has seen this before: Katie Ledecky won Olympic gold at 15 and Canada's Penny Oleksiak at 16. Some of those swimmers kept improving for years, while others plateaued as their bodies and training changed — so a record at 13 predicts potential, not a guaranteed career.

perspectives.perspective: Forward-looking — the road to Los Angeles
perspectives.description: The next three years will be about managing growth, training load and school rather than chasing every record. Her team must decide how many international meets she swims and which strokes she specialises in, while rivals like Summer McIntosh set the pace she is chasing.
